newsitem.title: SOMALIA: At least 26 killed in Somali fighting.
newsitem.headline: At least 26 killed in Somali fighting.

text.p: At least 26 people were killed and 48 wounded on Wednesday when forces of Somali faction leader Ali Hassan Osman Atto captured an airstrip from militiamen of his rival Hussein Aideed, witnesses said.

They said Osman Atto's militiamen attacked Aideed's forces at the Middle Shabelle airstrip, 50 km (30 miles) from Mogadishu. They captured the airstrip in the attack involving eight "technical" four-wheel-drive battlewagons.

Abdi Osman, a man wounded in the fighting and taken to the Hassan Jiis Memorial Hospital in Mogadishu, said Atto's militiamen shot at anything in sight at the strip -- used mainly by suppliers of the mild stimulant qat from neighbouring Kenya.
Osman said an Indian pilot who had landed in his Cessna plane carrying qat was captured and his plane was hit. He said 26 people were killed and 48 were wounded including himself.

On Tuesday, 13 people were killed and eight others wounded in an attack by unidentified militiamen in an area inhabited by Hussein Aideed supporters south of Mogadishu. No one has claimed responsibility for the attack.
The fighting this week was the most violent flareup since Somali factions -- including Atto and Aideed -- agreed in Nairobi two weeks ago to end hostilities and remove all roadblocks.
